items: Without a release, a string is what it means today …
Across an assembly change, places are compared through Ensembl's own mapping of the two assemblies, and only where Ensembl publishes one.
Copies on patches and alternative loci are placed by Ensembl's assembly exceptions.
A string of digits is read in every database whose ids are numbers.
A gene's own continuation does not outrank a branch that left it while it lived on.
An id that Ensembl's history carries to another place answers that id, and the result does not say that the gene moved.
An id that Ensembl retired and later brought back with an old version is one node with two lives.
An Ensembl id that names a transcript at some releases and a translation at others is one node.
At its own release, a symbol of the organism's name authority can answer another gene …
A string is read in every name source and database the graph holds at the release read, so the answer holds every gene that any of them gives it.
A name in one letter case that a link of another gene spells exactly so answers that gene, not the gene the name authority displays with it in mixed case.
Where an organism's symbols are written in capitals, a symbol typed with small letters can answer another gene whose synonym is spelt so.
Where Ensembl's history gives a gene no successor, an answer is the gene a bridge reaches, which no record of Ensembl states.
A gene that Ensembl retired without a successor can answer another gene than the one that holds its accessions today.
A gene whose history splits, converted to an external database, answers no identifier where the first-ranked of its descendants has none, although another descendant has one.
Where Ensembl's history splits a gene, the best answer is ranked by Ensembl's scores and the evidence of the candidates, not by which successor lies where the old gene lay.
In mouse releases 80 and 81, RefSeq_mRNA also holds predicted and RefSeqGene accessions.
The support of a name counts a database that writes it in another letter case.
A suffix of single-cell tools after a name that is no symbol of the name authority at the release asked about can be read into another gene's synonym.
An LRG record's gene id of the GRCh37 releases answers the gene the record describes, but its result lists that gene among the copies set apart, and not the record.
Low-9 quotation marks are not read as quotes.
Identifiers of databases that the graph does not hold answer nothing.
At mouse releases 48 to 54, a gene whose MGI symbol was its Havana id has no MGI symbol in a conversion.
The graph holds miRBase's names and accessions on genes of a miRNA biotype only, and leaves out an entry that Ensembl gives to genes at two loci.
A few synonyms are fragments of UniProt's evidence text.
An identifier of another database answers the gene Ensembl's cross-references give it, also where the database's own file says otherwise.
